article.title: Grok Bot x Muse x Duet x Dots x Hermes x OpenClaw: what makes each one different

data.text: GrokBot v.s Muse vs Dots vs Duet https://t.co/NKZqwtLEtx

Perplexity Teammates vs OpenAI Dots vs Claude Duet. All three just launched always-on agents that keep working while you sleep. If you could only keep one workflow agent, which one? A) Perplexity B) OpenAI C) Claude

note_tweet.text:
AGENT EDGE — Nov 10, 2026

Theme: agents become armies, and armies need managers. The stack is now orchestrators, cheap workers and a kill switch.

1. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Fable can act as an Orchestrator that hands simpler work to smaller models. $8/$40 per million tokens; fast mode is $16/$80. Anthropic says 1,000 Fable agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours, and 1,000+ subagents built a bootable OS in eight days. Fable is available today; Mythos needs a verification program. Why it matters: the flagship is now a manager. Swarm results are company demos.

2. Meta launched Muse Ember, a $0.10/$0.50 "worker" meant to pair with Muse Wonder or Spark. Available on the Model API and in Muse Code. Why it matters: the cheap half of the orchestrator/worker pattern is now a product.

3. OpenAI published Control Room, a kill switch for research inference. It says it can halt model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene, is already deployed internally, and fails closed. Announced, not a customer product. Why it matters: as fleets scale, the control plane matters as much as the model.

4. OpenAI dots can now connect several of your computers and pick which one runs a task. Why it matters: one personal agent, many machines.

THE EDGE
Swarms need managers: cheaper workers, clearer handoffs and a way to stop the work. Set the rules before the swarm invents a bureaucracy.
